nodes.title: 策略梯度
nodes.summary: Differentiate expected return through action log probabilities rather than environment dynamics.
nodes.definition: Policy-gradient methods optimize a parameterized policy using trajectory samples and derivatives of action log probabilities. The score-function identity permits this without differentiating the transition dynamics. A return or action-value estimate weights each score gradient; a state-dependent baseline can reduce variance without changing the expected gradient under the appropriate sampling assumptions. Finite samples can still have high variance, and an approximate critic can introduce estimation error. This method differs from supervised action imitation because updates weight actions by estimated future outcomes rather than simply matching demonstrated actions.
nodes.example: Run a stochastic control policy in simulation, record rewards, and assign reward-to-go estimates to sampled actions. Actions associated with above-baseline outcomes receive different update weights from below-baseline actions. Evaluate across seeds and held-out conditions; a positive sampled gradient step does not guarantee a higher true return.
nodes.role_en: Provides the derivation behind actor–critic and PPO, and a model-free contrast to differentiating through a world model.

notation.meaning: Trajectory sampled using the policy and environment.
Return-minus-baseline or advantage estimate; unbiasedness depends on its construction.
Differentiable stochastic action distribution.

nodes.title: 时序差分与自举
nodes.summary: Use a learned next-state value inside a prediction target.
nodes.definition: Temporal-difference learning updates a value estimate using rewards and another current value estimate. This use of an estimated future value is called bootstrapping. A one-step TD residual compares the current value with an immediate reward plus discounted next-state value. Terminal states require correct masking; a time-limit truncation may have different semantics from a true terminal event. Bootstrapping can reduce variance relative to full-return targets but introduces dependence on the accuracy and stability of current estimates. Nonlinear approximation, off-policy sampling and bootstrapping together require particular care.
nodes.example: At one transition, combine the observed reward with the estimated value of the next state and update the current-state value toward that target. When an episode truly terminates, omit the continuation value. Confusing a timeout with task termination can systematically bias the learned value.
nodes.role_en: Connects Bellman equations to actor–critic, Q-learning, DQN, SAC and advantage estimation.

notation.meaning: True-terminal indicator for this target convention.
One-step TD error.
Discount factor.

nodes.title: 同策略与异策略数据
nodes.summary: Distinguish the policy that collected observations from the policy being evaluated or improved.
nodes.definition: On-policy methods use data matched to the relevant current policy, while off-policy methods can learn about a target policy from data collected by a different behavior policy. This distinction concerns data and update semantics, not whether training happens on a robot or simulator. Importance ratios can correct some action-distribution mismatches when support and estimator assumptions hold, but large or compounded ratios can create high variance. Other off-policy algorithms use Bellman consistency or different corrections. An off-policy-capable algorithm can still interact online; offline learning additionally forbids collecting new environment transitions during training.
nodes.example: A replay buffer contains actions from earlier exploratory policies. The current policy is different, so simply treating these trajectories as current-policy Monte Carlo samples is generally invalid. A Q-learning update can use off-policy transitions through its own target structure; an ordinary policy-gradient estimate needs an appropriate correction.
nodes.role_en: Clarifies replay reuse, SAC, PPO likelihood ratios and the stronger restrictions of offline RL.

notation.meaning: Behavior policy that collected the action.
Target policy.
Action-probability or density ratio where behavior support is sufficient; not by itself a complete correction for every objective.

nodes.title: 经验回放与目标网络
nodes.summary: Data reuse and slowly changing targets address different sources of instability.
nodes.definition: Experience replay stores environment transitions and samples them for learning, allowing data reuse and changing the temporal correlation pattern of minibatches. A target network supplies comparatively slow-changing predictions in bootstrapped targets, using periodic copies or moving-average parameter updates. These are separate mechanisms that can be combined. Replay sampling does not automatically remove distribution bias, and target networks do not ensure convergence. Buffer age, coverage, termination fields, priorities and update-to-data ratio affect training. Whether replay is valid depends on the learning rule; it cannot be added indiscriminately to an on-policy estimator.
nodes.example: Store state, action, reward, next state and termination information, sample a minibatch, and compute a TD target using frozen target parameters. Update the online network and then apply the configured target-update rule. Test data fields and masks before interpreting a low TD loss as successful control.
nodes.role_en: Supplies practical DQN/SAC training components and distinguishes a TD target network from a JEPA representation target encoder.

notation.meaning: Target-network parameters.
Moving-average coefficient; periodic hard copies are an alternative.
Replay buffer distribution, not necessarily the current policy distribution.

sources.title: CS285 Spring 2026 Section 4: DQN and SAC

nodes.title: 深度 Q 网络
nodes.summary: Approximate discrete-action values with a neural network and fit Bellman targets.
nodes.definition: DQN uses a neural network to approximate action values and learns from sampled transitions using Q-learning-style targets. A replay buffer reuses observations, and a separate target network slows target changes in the widely used formulation. The greedy action maximizes estimated Q among a finite action set; exploration uses an additional collecting strategy. This discrete maximization is unsuitable for directly enumerating high-dimensional continuous joint commands. Function approximation and bootstrapping can produce unstable or biased values, and low prediction loss is not equivalent to good policy return. Variants such as Double DQN make additional changes.
nodes.example: A robot selects among a small set of validated high-level skills using estimated Q values. The low-level skill controllers remain responsible for execution. This differs from using DQN to enumerate every possible vector of joint torques, which would make the action set impractically large.
nodes.role_en: Provides the canonical deep value-learning baseline before off-policy continuous actor–critic algorithms.

notation.meaning: Online and target Q-network parameters.
Stop-gradient operator for the fitted target.
True-terminal indicator; squared loss shown as a basic form, with robust alternatives used in practice.

sources.title: CS285 Spring 2026 Section 4: DQN and SAC
Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning

nodes.title: 优势函数与 GAE
nodes.summary: Compare an action with the state baseline and combine multi-step TD residuals.
nodes.definition: The advantage function compares an action value with the value of the state under the same policy. Generalized advantage estimation forms a discounted sum of TD residuals to construct a practical policy-gradient weight. Its lambda parameter controls how strongly longer-horizon residuals contribute, changing bias and variance when the value function is approximate. Implementations must correctly handle episode boundaries, true termination and truncated rollouts. Normalizing a batch of advantages is an additional implementation choice, not the mathematical definition. A favorable estimated advantage does not establish that a physical action is safe or optimal.
nodes.example: For a PPO rollout, compute value estimates and TD residuals, then accumulate them backward with the chosen discount and lambda. Stop or bootstrap according to the actual boundary semantics. Comparing several lambda values requires measuring return and variability, rather than assuming the longest estimate is always best.
nodes.role_en: Makes the advantage term in policy gradients and PPO explicit and links critic error to policy updates.

notation.meaning: Trace parameter in [0,1].
TD residual with the appropriate boundary mask.
Finite rollout boundary; required bootstrap handling is assumed.

nodes.title: 软演员评论家
nodes.summary: Off-policy actor–critic optimizes reward together with policy entropy.
nodes.definition: Soft actor–critic is an off-policy actor–critic family based on maximum-entropy reinforcement learning. It fits soft action values from replay data and improves a stochastic policy using both expected value and log-probability terms. Common modern continuous-control implementations use two Q functions, target critics, reparameterized action sampling and a temperature controlling entropy; these details should be distinguished from every historical version. Action bounds and distribution transformations require correct probability-density handling. Replay reuse can improve sample use, but neither entropy regularization nor the algorithm establishes safe exploration or guaranteed convergence.
nodes.example: A simulated controller learns continuous action targets using replayed transitions and a stochastic policy. During deployment, the chosen deterministic or stochastic execution convention affects behavior. Compare environment steps, wall-clock compute and physical success separately when evaluating SAC against an on-policy PPO baseline.
nodes.role_en: Provides a core continuous-control alternative to PPO and links off-policy learning to entropy-based control inference.

notation.meaning: Entropy temperature in a common modern SAC actor objective.
Twin learned critics.
Replay-state distribution; minimize this actor loss.

sources.title: CS285 Spring 2026 Section 4: DQN and SAC

nodes.title: 基于模型的强化学习
nodes.summary: Learn or use transition predictions to improve decisions, not merely to forecast observations.
nodes.definition: Model-based reinforcement learning uses a dynamics model to support policy improvement or action selection. A learned model can predict compact states, latent representations, observations or rewards; these choices change training data needs and planning costs. Some methods optimize actions through rollouts and execute the first action, while others train a policy or critic using imagined data. Model fitting alone is not yet an RL solution. Planning can exploit model errors outside data support, and long rollouts compound mistakes. Closed-loop replanning, uncertainty handling and real-environment evaluation address different parts of this problem.
nodes.example: Fit a compact next-state predictor from simulator transitions, use it to score candidate short action sequences, and execute one step before observing again. Compare the realized transition with the prediction. A low average one-step error does not ensure that optimized action sequences remain accurate near contacts.
nodes.role_en: Forms the stable prerequisite bridge to world-model planning papers, PETS, MBPO, Dreamer and TD-MPC.

notation.meaning: Chosen dynamics predictor; stochastic and latent variants need appropriate rollout semantics.
Planning horizon.
Predicted or known task reward; expression illustrates model-predictive action selection.

nodes.title: 离线强化学习
nodes.summary: Optimize decision quality from a fixed dataset without collecting new training transitions.
nodes.definition: Offline reinforcement learning learns a policy from a fixed dataset of transitions or trajectories, without new environment interaction during that training phase. It differs from behavior cloning because it uses return-related structure to evaluate or improve actions rather than only matching demonstrated actions. The learned policy can choose actions poorly supported by the data, causing value extrapolation error and distribution shift. Conservative values, behavior constraints and policy extraction rules address this in different ways. Offline evaluation is itself difficult without appropriate support or assumptions. Off-policy capability alone does not make an ordinary online algorithm robust in this setting.
nodes.example: A robot has recorded successful and failed motion episodes, but training cannot request new trials. A learned critic may assign high value to an unrecorded action that it has never evaluated physically. Test support, tuning protocol and deployment outcomes rather than selecting a policy only by its predicted training-set value.
nodes.role_en: Clarifies offline datasets in world models and VLA pipelines and the offline-to-online bridge used in modern robot learning.

notation.meaning: Fixed training data with no new interactions during offline training.
An offline learning procedure; formula alone does not specify a valid algorithm.

sources.title: Conservative Q-Learning for Offline Reinforcement Learning

nodes.title: 探索与内在奖励
nodes.summary: Collect informative experience while respecting task and physical constraints.
nodes.definition: Exploration concerns how an agent gathers experience needed to improve decisions. Random action noise, entropy regularization, novelty bonuses, uncertainty-directed behavior and goal-conditioned exploration make different assumptions and can lead to different coverage. An intrinsic reward can supplement task reward, but novelty may track sensor noise or uncontrollable events rather than useful discoveries. Information gain and reward improvement are different objectives. Simulation exploration can use resets unavailable on hardware, so a data-collection strategy must be evaluated within actual constraints. No novelty or entropy bonus by itself establishes safe real-world exploration.
nodes.example: A soccer controller repeatedly sees only stationary-ball situations. Adding noise may produce varied actions but few useful contact examples. A structured collection scheme can target underrepresented valid states. Inspect coverage and failures directly, while keeping physical limits and recovery capability separate from the training reward.
nodes.role_en: Connects entropy, uncertainty and active perception to experience collection and multi-task robot learning.

notation.meaning: Chosen intrinsic bonus; not necessarily a calibrated information measure.
Weight between task reward and the auxiliary bonus.

nodes.title: 控制的概率推断视角
nodes.summary: Relate reward-seeking policies to probabilistic optimality variables and entropy-regularized objectives.
nodes.definition: Control as inference introduces probabilistic variables representing desirable outcomes and relates their likelihood to reward. Inference over trajectories then suggests policy-learning objectives, often including entropy or a policy-prior divergence term. This is a modeling construction, not a claim that every controller literally performs exact Bayesian inference. Dynamics constraints matter: freely tilting an entire stochastic trajectory distribution can alter transition behavior that the controller cannot choose. Variational formulations restrict the policy-induced distribution and yield tractable objectives under specified assumptions. This view helps connect maximum-entropy RL, approximate inference and generative decision methods.
nodes.example: A policy receives reward for reaching a target while retaining entropy in its action distribution. The probabilistic formulation explains why the objective may contain both reward and log-policy terms. It still requires explicit transition assumptions, reward scaling and a practical learning algorithm such as a soft actor–critic method.
nodes.role_en: Connects variational reasoning to maximum-entropy control and later generative/world-model planning research.
nodes.latex: J(\pi)=\mathbb E_{\tau\sim p_\pi}\!\left[\sum_t r(s_t,a_t)+\alpha\mathcal H(\pi(\cdot\mid s_t))\right]

notation.meaning: Trajectory distribution with environment dynamics fixed and actions selected by the policy.
Entropy weight; reference-policy formulations replace entropy by a divergence term.

nodes.title: 语义、实例与全景分割
nodes.summary: Pixel labels and object-instance identities answer different visual questions.
nodes.definition: Image segmentation predicts regions or labels at pixel resolution. Semantic segmentation assigns a category to each pixel without distinguishing individual objects of the same category. Instance segmentation separates individual object masks, while panoptic segmentation combines category coverage with instance identities according to a defined labeling convention. These outputs differ from bounding-box detection and require matching annotation and evaluation procedures. Pixel-level confidence is not geometric certainty, especially near boundaries, transparent surfaces or occlusion. A mask supports downstream geometry only when associated camera measurements and calibration are valid; it does not reveal hidden object surfaces.
nodes.example: Two players occupy the same image. A semantic map labels both as person, while instance masks assign separate identities to their visible regions. A ball mask can guide depth selection, but occluded ball surfaces remain unobserved. Report boundary and small-object errors alongside any global pixel metric.
nodes.role_en: Fills a core CS231n perception prerequisite connecting visual recognition to object-centric geometry, tracking and interaction.

notation.meaning: Predicted and reference pixel sets for a specified class or matched instance.
Intersection over union; multi-class, instance and panoptic evaluation add their own aggregation and matching conventions.

Object detection provides a useful comparison between boxes and pixel masks.
Each segmentation task needs compatible labels and metrics.
